clue.text: Infernal food, as served, has no good ingredient

indicators.note: a dish that has something as an ingredient holds it within itself

blocks.note: food as it is served up is a dish
what is no good is evil

explanation.surface: A hellish meal from which every decent ingredient has been left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no good ingredient' reads as a dish lacking anything wholesome, but it means the dish contains wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something devilish is fiendish, worthy of the devil, just as infernal describes what belongs to hell.

clue.text: Satan captured 500 we have to infer

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor

blocks.note: the deuce is an old name for the devil
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: We must conclude the devil took five hundred prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What the deuce?' uses deuce as an old euphemism for the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce is to reason to a conclusion from evidence, the same as to infer.

clue.text: Show indecision leave premises, sick at heart

indicators.note: at heart puts one thing in the middle of the other

blocks.note: to vacate is to leave a building
sick means ill

explanation.surface: Someone dithering over leaving a building while feeling unwell inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacillate is to waver between options, the way a person unable to decide behaves.

clue.text: Despicable dope

blocks.note: first meaning: an adjective, mean and contemptible
second meaning: a noun, the inside information

explanation.walkthrough: Dope looks like an insult to sit with despicable, but here it is slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means base or contemptible, and the noun is slang for the inside story or facts.

clue.text: Mistakes made by mouthpiece on board

indicators.note: on board means aboard a ship, so the word goes inside the ship's letters

blocks.note: lip is cheek or backchat, what a mouthpiece delivers
a steamship, SS, as in the crossword convention for on board

explanation.surface: Errors made by a spokesman while aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Being on board puts something between S and S, the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Slips are small errors, like slips of the tongue, so the word is a near synonym.

clue.text: Symbol appears to resemble meaning, but not all of it

indicators.note: only part of the run of words is taken, so the answer lies inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of resemble and the start of meaning

explanation.surface: A sign seems to resemble its meaning, though only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is hidden in resEMBLE Meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem is a device or badge standing for an idea, which is what a symbol is.

clue.text: Pin-up held by masculine type Roman soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from the bottom, so backwards
what is held by something sits inside it

blocks.note: a masculine type is a male
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pin-up picture kept by a macho legionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pin-up' looks like one word for a poster girl; split, it is the word reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A maniple was a subdivision of the Roman legion, a company of soldiers.

clue.text: The game of many a Holy Roman Emperor

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, a crossword stand-in for many
several Holy Roman Emperors were named Otto

explanation.surface: A pastime favoured by numerous medieval emperors.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance like bingo, played by matching drawn numbers on cards.

clue.text: Threatening main disruption to railway

indicators.note: disruption throws things into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: main rearranged
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A menacing major disruption to the rail network.
explanation.definitionFit: Minatory is a formal word meaning menacing, expressing a threat.

clue.text: The cheapest way to travel is always in coach

indicators.note: in places one thing inside the other

blocks.note: a stagecoach, shortened to stage
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: Budget travel always means going by coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like the cheap way to travel, but it is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the lowest-priced passenger class on a ship, the cheapest berth available.

clue.text: One "returning" to capital fortune and fame

definitions.text: One "returning" to capital fortune and fame

blocks.clueFragment: One "returning" to capital fortune and fame
blocks.note: surface reading: someone heading back to the city to make money and a name
setter's reading: the pantomime hero heard the bells say 'Turn again' and went back to London, where he became rich and Lord Mayor

explanation.surface: Someone coming back to the capital to find wealth and renown.
explanation.walkthrough: In the legend, Bow Bells called 'Turn again, Whittington, Lord Mayor of London', so he turned back; the quotation marks flag that famous turning.
explanation.definitionFit: The story's hero went back to London and won fortune and fame as its mayor, exactly as described.

clue.text: Ring us up about nothing? How insensitive!

indicators.note: about means around, so the earlier words surround what follows

blocks.note: to ring up is to call, followed by us as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone hurt that nobody phones them about anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a complaint about not being phoned, but the exclamation itself is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Callous means unfeeling and hard-hearted, so a callous act is the very thing the exclamation complains of.

clue.text: Take advantage of a great achievement

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to use for one's own gain
second meaning: a noun, a bold or heroic deed

explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs the two meanings together as if seizing an opportunity; one is the verb, the other the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as a verb for profiting unfairly from something and a noun for a daring feat.

clue.text: Show Boat flower-girl in this state of Mississippi

blocks.note: first meaning: the heroine of the musical Show Boat, a girl named after a flower
second meaning: the tree whose name is Mississippi's nickname, the ___ State, and its state flower

explanation.surface: A girl selling flowers aboard the showboat on the Mississippi.
explanation.walkthrough: Show Boat is set on Mississippi riverboats, so the two meanings sit naturally together.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnolia Hawks is the musical's heroine, and the magnolia is Mississippi's official flower, giving the Magnolia State nickname.

clue.text: Entry of inferior press into royal reception obtained by purchase

indicators.note: an entry into something goes inside it

blocks.note: a levee was a monarch's morning reception
a rag is a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: Tabloid journalists bought their way into a palace reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' looks like buying; here it is the mechanical sense of grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase also means a firm hold or mechanical advantage, the force multiplier a lever provides.

clue.text: No red ruin where Samuel's spirit was raised

indicators.note: a ruin is something wrecked, so the letters are knocked about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A place with no red ruins, where a ghost was once summoned.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible, Saul had the witch of Endor call up the spirit of the dead prophet Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: The First Book of Samuel sets the seance at Endor, home of the medium Saul consulted.

clue.text: Left after record party on our soil

blocks.note: a disco is a party with recorded music
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: What was left behind after a party on our land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soil' looks like earth; it is the verb meaning to stain. 'Left' looks like a verb too, but it is the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To discolour something is to stain or spoil its colour, which is what soiling does.

clue.text: Does a fellow provide a meal for him?

definitions.text: Does a fellow provide a meal for him?

blocks.clueFragment: Does a fellow provide a meal for him?
blocks.note: surface reading: whether a friend cooks dinner for someone
setter's reading: the fellow human is himself the meal

explanation.surface: Asking whether a friend lays on dinner for a guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provide a meal' suggests cooking; the dark joke is that the fellow is the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater dines on other people, so a fellow human literally supplies his food.

clue.text: About to complete perm?

indicators.note: what is needed to complete a word is that word with its given start taken away

blocks.note: a perm is short for a permanent wave

explanation.surface: A hairdresser about to finish off a perm.
explanation.walkthrough: PERM plus ANENT makes PERMANENT, so ANENT is what completes it. The question mark flags the playful wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Anent is an old or Scottish preposition meaning concerning, regarding, on the subject of.

clue.text: Timeless 14 underfoot causes revolution

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining a noun, fair as the clue reads 'it causes revolution'

blocks.note: first meaning: 14 without its age is a lever, and this one is worked by the foot
second meaning: the device that turns a wheel round on a spinning wheel or lathe

explanation.surface: Something lasting, trampled underfoot, sparks a political revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is LEVERAGE; timeless removes AGE, leaving a lever. Revolution means a wheel turning, not an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-operated lever that drives the wheel of a sewing machine or lathe round.

clue.text: Like Johann Strauss having to contend with three different directions

blocks.note: to vie is to contend
north, north-east and south-east

explanation.surface: The waltz king pulled three ways at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The three directions are N, NE and SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Strauss was born and worked in Vienna, so he and his music are Viennese by origin.

clue.text: One's out of line perhaps with the boss of this plant

indicators.note: out of line means not in proper order, so the letters are jumbled
the head of the plant is set aside, the leading letter dropped

blocks.note: one, its 's read as is
what is out of line is perhaps out of plumb, not vertical

explanation.surface: Something out of line, perhaps with whoever runs the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose clue: out of line suggests out of PLUMB; drop its head, the P of plant, and rearrange the rest with ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelumbo is the botanical genus of the lotus, so it names this very plant.

clue.text: Way up? Left to a snake to bring you down

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left

blocks.clueFragment: a snake to bring you down
blocks.note: an adder is a snake, like those that send you down in the board game

explanation.surface: A game of snakes and ladders: one climbs, the other sends you back.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder is a means of climbing, a route to a higher place.

clue.text: Uncle wandering by a river shows such energy

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective describing such energy

indicators.note: wandering means straying from a fixed course, so the letters move about

blocks.note: uncle rearranged
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An uncle strolling beside a river radiates vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places A and R after the shuffled uncle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear energy comes from the atomic nucleus, so nuclear names that kind of power.

clue.text: Instrument for a bit of battery, nothing more

blocks.note: a battery is made up of cells
nothing is zero, the letter O, added on

explanation.surface: A musical instrument needing just a little battery power and nothing else.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a large bowed string instrument of the violin family.

clue.text: Something alarming, taking on a war goddess

blocks.note: an alarm is sounded by a bell
the word on, taken as written after taking
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something frightening taking on a goddess of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link joining the bell to the words that follow, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellona was the Roman goddess of war, sister or wife of Mars.

clue.text: Morning massage up in the country

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from the bottom, so backwards

blocks.note: a.m. marks the morning
a rub is a massage

explanation.surface: A morning massage taken somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Burma is the former name of Myanmar, the South-East Asian nation.

clue.text: Peterson's opponent, one of a tenacious breed

blocks.note: first meaning: the hero who fought the master criminal Carl Peterson in Sapper's thrillers
second meaning: a bulldog, a breed famous for hanging on, which gave the hero his nickname

explanation.surface: An adversary described as coming from a stubborn family line.
explanation.walkthrough: Carl Peterson is the arch-villain of the 1920s novels by Sapper; the hero's nickname is a dog breed known for gripping and not letting go.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh 'Bulldog' Drummond is Peterson's nemesis, and his nickname makes him one of the bulldog breed.

clue.text: Boy's terribly ill, swallowing one

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are disordered
what swallows something takes it inside itself

blocks.note: ill rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lad is very poorly after swallowing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly ill' looks like the boy's condition, but it is the wordplay; the 's is just 'is' joining definition to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionel is a boy's first name, so it is an example of a boy.

clue.text: Worker of Open University in barrel construction

indicators.note: in places one thing within the other
construction means building something new out of the parts

blocks.note: barrel rearranged
OU is the standard abbreviation for the Open University

explanation.surface: An Open University student who works as a cooper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is Britain's distance-learning university, and OU is its standard short form.
explanation.definitionFit: A labourer is a manual worker, so the hyponym fits the general term.
